l.i: Iehouah armipotens, beatus homo, qui confidit in te.

main_text.l: Est Epiphonema, quo propheta noster significat, eos demum felices esse, qui in vno Deo confidunt.
Beati sunt, qui in eo vno fiduciam suam collocant, qui illos nō tantùm creauit, sed etiam redemit è potestate tenebrarum, & transtulit in regnum lucis.
Atqui Dominus Deus noster, is ipse est. Dicitur enim Iehouah, etiā hac ob causam quòd in eo vno sumus, viuimus & mouemur.
Dicitur etiam armipotens, non ideò solùm quòd ei militant omnes creaturæ, sed etiam, quia carnales & spirituales hostes nostros, ipse vnus debellet & vincit, vt ne nobis nocere possint.
Quare beati sunt qui in eo solo confidunt. Optimum est, fide in Deo solo ac-quiescere, vt in summo nostro bono. Pessimum autem est, fiduciam in creaturis collocare.
Ac-quiescere: the catchword "ac-" at the foot continues the word on the next page.

page.notes: The first letter of "confidit" in the verse quotation is faint and may be a long s or c; it is transcribed as "confidit" with no mark, but it is doubtful. The word "fumus" in the printed line "quod in eo uno sumus" is read as "sumus", with the long s taken as a plain s. The first word "Quare" stands in the margin area at the start of its paragraph and is read as the paragraph opening. The marginal label "Thesis.1." is printed with a stop before the numeral, and "Thesis 2." with a space. The words "De efficiente & finali." are a side note beside the paragraph that continues onto the next page. The paragraph "Fides in eo" ends the page mid-sentence; the catchword is "ac-".
